subject: octopus
pitch: A curious reef octopus in coral and rust tones, covered in little bumps and paler mottling. A soft, bulbous head, golden eyes with bar-shaped pupils and a slightly grumpy brow. Its eight arms curl out in every direction, each lined with rows of cream suckers, and one arm proudly holds up an old brass key it found on a shipwreck.
reasoning:
I'm uncertain about the exact SDK signatures, so to minimize risk I'm leaning toward relying mostly on plain three.js geometry rather than guessing at unknown builder options.

I'll go with plain THREE meshes parented to the root for geometry, paired with joints/chains for the skeleton, even though it won't be truly skinned—reliability matters more than a perfect rig. For the tentacles I'm writing a custom tapered tube function using a Catmull-Rom curve with Frenet frames and low-poly flat shading, plus small spheres and cylinders for suckers and head bumps, and I'm sketching out the overall proportions for the mantle and arm placement.

Now I'm laying out the body proportions: a scaled sphere for the mantle, a bulbous head tilted back, golden eyes with horizontal bar pupils and angled brows for a grumpy look, positioned symmetrically on the body surface near the front.

Working out the arm geometry now - each arm starts at radius 0.22 near the base and curls outward to radius 0.9, with the tube height following a curve that stays low near the body then lifts at the tips, and the tube radius tapering from 0.075 down to 0.008 along its length.

For the key arm specifically, I'm planning it to extend outward to radius 0.55 then rise up to height 0.85, ending in a tip that holds a vertical key shape - a torus ring at the top with a shaft and teeth boxes below, positioned so the curling tip wraps naturally around the shaft.

For suckers, since Frenet frames get unstable on a mostly horizontal curve, I'm computing a horizontal side vector from tangent crossed with up, then placing sucker rows offset along that side direction with a slight downward tilt so they face somewhat toward the camera rather than straight down.

Each sucker is just two cylinders—a cream outer disc and a darker inner disc—oriented using a quaternion from the up axis to the desired direction, keeping it to 2 meshes per sucker. I'm tightening the counts (arms × rows × suckers) to stay under the 1000-part budget, then adding scattered small spheres on the mantle for coral-colored mottling bumps.

Now I'm picking a cohesive palette of coral, rust, pale peach, cream, gold, and brass tones, with materials cached by color to avoid duplicates. I'm setting up the joint hierarchy starting with a root body joint and a head joint, then wrapping the tentacle chain calls in try/catch blocks in case the chain API requires stricter parenting than I'm assuming.

Writing tube geometry code...

I'll build my own deterministic LCG for bump randomness instead of trusting the external rng to be callable. Now I'm laying out the eight arm curves at 45° increments, with the key-holding arm specially shaped: its shaft rises vertically to a bow-shaped ring near the top.

Working out the key's dimensions now—shaft running from roughly y=0.8 to 1.3, teeth jutting out near the bottom around y=0.82-0.92, and the bow ring sitting at the very top, with the arm's final curl point positioned to visually grip the shaft.

Now I'm defining the radius taper for each ground arm and computing their positions using angle and radius functions that vary by arm index, with alternating tip lifts to give them different poses extending down toward the body base.

I'm adding a skirt cone geometry beneath the mantle to fill the gap where the arms attach, sizing it so the top radius matches the body's bottom curve. Then I'm placing gold eyeball spheres with small pupil boxes offset along an outward-facing normal direction on the front of the head.

Now I'm working out brow positioning: rust-colored flattened spheres tilted to give a grumpy expression, rotating each brow outward-up so the outer edge lifts higher than the inner edge, mirrored for left and right eyes, positioned slightly overlapping the top of each eye. Next I'm starting on a small funnel-shaped mouth or siphon cone near the front-bottom of the head.
